limitations: Safe paste still rejects occupied destinations. The original desktop overwrite planner exists; an explicit overwrite choice and its loss/linked-track qualification remain required before closing the complete clip-paste parity row.
The original v1 clipboard text has no top-level crossing list. The trusted current-session clipboard retains its cached crossings; nested timeline crossings stay native.
Clipboard image import is a separate unsupported path; this increment implements native text clips/media only.

Native file fingerprints use canonical path, size and mtime, not a cryptographic content digest. External claimed fingerprints are replaced with values computed from authorized root files; source entry/ctime witnesses guard preparation through apply.

The first finite API attempt restored modified test bytes but not their mtime, invalidating native file fingerprints before an unrelated current-copy no-op check. The fixture now restores original mtime; production source was unchanged.

The first Windows pass found Ctrl+C was not reaching the keydown-only adapter. Native DOM copy/cut events and duplicate suppression were then added; real Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V and Ctrl+X passed in the final browser, with exactly one DeleteClips and native Undo.
Root4MiB/4096 selection/64 file/64 timeline and shared256 descriptor bounds apply. Each native probe is isolated20s/512MiB/CPU10; whole600s parser processing is cooperative.
This metadata-only qualification does not establish rendered/GPU/physical audio/native bitmap clipboard or general shortcut/DPI/release acceptance.
The main editor stays on its earlier binary, preserving all five unsaved MoveClips and Undo; the verified candidate is staged separately.
